title: Apps
description: The apps your employees build: a preview of each at its own address on your server, and, once a client is ready, its live site at the client's own domain. A deploy takes an exact commit; if anything fails, the version that ran before keeps running.
stopAllConfirm: Stop every running preview in this workspace? Each one can be started again with one click.
stopAllDone: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing was running.} one {Stopping # preview.} other {Stopping # previews.}}
readOnly: Only Admins and Owners deploy, stop or change apps.

statusMessage.idle: Stopped after {days} days without a new release.
statusMessage.server_full: Not started: the server already runs as many previews as it allows. Stop another one first.
statusMessage.no_release: Not started: this app has no deployed version yet.
statusMessage.kill_switch: Refused: the kill switch is on.
statusMessage.server_unavailable: The server could not be reached. Check it in Settings → Servers.
statusMessage.health_failed: The app did not answer its health check, so it was stopped.
statusMessage.stop_failed: Stopping failed. See the latest log and try again.
statusMessage.start_failed: Starting failed. See the latest log and try again.
statusMessage.remove_failed: Removing it from the server failed. Try again once the server is reachable.
statusMessage.rollback_failed: The new version failed and going back to the previous one failed too. Deploy again or roll back by hand.
statusMessage.interrupted: A deploy was cut off by a restart. Check the app and deploy again.
statusMessage.firewall_off: The apps firewall is not running on the server, so nothing was started. Re-run prepare.sh or check wfos-apps-firewall.service there.
statusMessage.no_database_cluster: The server has no apps database yet. Re-run prepare.sh on it.
statusMessage.restart_failed: The new version failed, and the previous one did not start again. Start it again or deploy a fix.
statusMessage.env_forbidden: Not started: some of the app's environment variables are set by the platform. Remove them in the app's settings.
statusMessage.restore_failed: Restoring the database failed and the app did not come back healthy, so the maintenance page stays on. See the log, then restore again or deploy a fix.
statusMessage.restoring: Restoring the database from a backup; the maintenance page is shown meanwhile.

list.running: {count, plural, =0 {none running} one {# running} other {# running}}
list.modulesWaiting: {count, plural, one {# PRD to approve} other {# PRDs to approve}}

empty.title: No apps yet
empty.lead: An app here is a preview of a repository: Workforce OS builds one commit on your server and puts it online at its own address, behind a password.
empty.step1Help: Settings → Servers. The server gives every app an address under its domain.
empty.step1Done: {count, plural, one {# server ready} other {# servers ready}}
empty.step2Done: {count, plural, one {# repository connected} other {# repositories connected}}
empty.step3Help: At the root of the repository, next to package.json. This is all a Next.js app needs; the rest has defaults:
empty.defaults: Defaults: install with pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, build with pnpm build, start with pnpm start on 127.0.0.1 and $PORT, a health check at /api/health, 512 MB of memory. Add "database": true for a PostgreSQL database (DATABASE_URL is set for you) and "migrate" for a migration command.

form.title: New app
form.description: The app gets its address now. Nothing runs on the server until the first deploy.
form.name: Name
form.slugHelp: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. It cannot be changed later.
form.slugInvalid: Use 2–30 lowercase letters, digits and single dashes, starting with a letter.
form.noServer: No ready server yet. Register and verify one in Settings → Servers first.
form.noRepository: No repository connected yet. An Owner connects one in Settings → Repositories.
form.branchHelp: A deploy takes this branch's latest commit unless you pick another one.
form.accessPasswordHelp: The browser asks for a username and password before showing anything. Recommended for previews.
form.accessPublicHelp: No password. Search engines are still asked not to index it.
form.created: App created. Deploy it when the repository is ready.

detail.notFound: This app does not exist (any more).
detail.nextDeploy: A running app gets the new access setting at once; a branch change applies at the next deploy.
detail.saved: Saved. Access applies at once to a running app; the branch at the next deploy.
detail.fixed: The subdomain, server and repository are fixed. To move an app, create a new one.
detail.dangerHelp: Deleting removes the app from its server with its files and its database, then from Workforce OS. You confirm with your password and authenticator code.
detail.deleteConfirm: Delete {name}? It is removed from its server together with its files and its database. This cannot be undone.
detail.deleting: Deleting the app from its server…
detail.deployingNote: A deploy is running. You can follow it in the log below.
detail.deployingLiveNote: A release to live is running. You can follow it in the log below.
detail.dangerHelpLive: Deleting removes the app from its servers, the preview and the live site, with their files and databases, then from Workforce OS. Only the Owner can: with the live site stopped, its domain typed, and password and authenticator code.
detail.deleteConfirmLive: Delete {name} with its live site at {domain}? Both environments are removed from their servers with their files and databases. This cannot be undone.
detail.deleteNeedsOwner: This app has a live site, so only the Owner can delete it.
detail.slotHelp: Live runs in one of two slots: a new version starts in the other one, then traffic switches over without cutting connections.
detail.backupStale: Over a day without a backup

actions.stopConfirm: Stop {name}? The address shows an error until it is started again.
actions.rollbackConfirm: Bring back {commit}? It runs as a new release. The database is not restored: the data stays as it is now.
actions.stopLiveConfirm: Stop the live site of {name}? {domain} shows an error to its visitors until it is started again.
actions.rollbackLiveConfirm: Bring back {commit} on the live site? It runs as a new live release. The live database is not restored: its data stays as it is now.

deploy.title: Deploy {name}
deploy.description: Builds one exact commit on {server}, checks it, then switches the address to it. If a step fails, the version running now stays.
deploy.audited: Your click is the decision: it is recorded in the audit log.
deploy.recentCommits: Commits that ran in the preview
deploy.neverDeployed: Not deployed to the preview yet
deploy.replaces: The preview now runs {branch} ({commit}: {subject}); this deploy replaces it.
deploy.notMerged: An agent's work stays on its own branch until it is merged, so {branch} may not have it yet.
deploy.sameBranch: The preview already runs {branch} at {commit}. Without a new commit on this branch the deploy is refused; pick another branch above to bring its work.

access.title: Preview password
access.description: The browser asks for this before it shows the preview. Share it only with the people who should see it.
access.public: This preview is open to anyone with the link.
access.rotateConfirm: Make a new password? A running preview switches to it within a minute and the old one stops working.
access.rotated: New password made. A running preview switches to it within a minute.
access.audited: Every time it is shown, the audit log records who looked.
access.liveDescription: The live site asks for this before it shows anything. Useful before launch; switch it to public in the live settings when the client goes live.
access.livePublic: The live site is public: anyone can open it, and search engines may index it.
access.liveOwnerOnly: Only the Owner sees or changes the live password.

env.title: Environment variables
env.description: Extra settings for the app, such as SMTP_HOST. Values are stored encrypted and never shown again; to change one, type a new value.
env.name: Name
env.saved: Variables saved. They apply at the next deploy.
env.nameInvalid: Use UPPER_CASE letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.
env.readOnly: Only Admins change variables. Names set now:
env.liveDescription: The live site's own settings: real SMTP, payment keys and the like. They are never shared with the preview, are stored encrypted and never shown again; they apply at the next release to live.
env.liveReadOnly: Only the Owner changes the live variables. Names set now:

releases.title: Releases
releases.empty: No release yet. The first deploy shows up here with its log.
releases.logWaiting: Waiting for the worker to start…
releases.noLogs: Logs are visible to Members and up.

warningHelp.first_publish: Nothing has run at this address yet: this becomes the app's first version.
warningHelp.manifest_changed: How the app is installed, built, started, migrated or checked differs from the version that runs now.
warningHelp.scripts_changed: The build and start commands in package.json changed, so the server may run something new.
warningHelp.new_database: The platform creates a PostgreSQL database for this app and gives it DATABASE_URL.
warningHelp.destructive_migration: A migration may drop or rewrite data. The database is backed up first, but read the migration before you approve.
warningHelp.public_access: The app is public: anyone with the link sees it, without a password.

taskPreviews.title: Previews
taskPreviews.waiting: The task waits here until the platform reports how the deploy went; the employee does not continue before that.

live.emptyLead: When the client is ready, the app goes live at the client's own domain, on a server of your choice, with its own variables and its own database. Previews never touch live data.
live.ownerOnly: Only the Owner sets up a live site.
live.setupDescription: Choose the server and the client's domain. Nothing is published yet: you first point the domain at the server, then release a version that ran in the preview.
live.serverHelp: A live server: meant for client sites.
live.serverDevHelp: This is a dev server. Fine for a test; for a client's real site, pick a server with the live role.
live.domainHelp: The address the client's visitors type, e.g. app.client.com. The client's DNS must point it at the server.
live.domainInvalid: Use a domain like app.example.com: lowercase letters, digits, dashes and dots.
live.domainPreview: {domain} is a preview address. A live site needs a domain of its own.
live.aliasesHelp: Up to {max} more names that redirect to the domain, such as www. Each needs the same DNS record.
live.setupNoteSeparate: Its own variables, password and database: nothing is copied from the preview.
live.setupNotePublic: Public by default and visible to search engines; you can put a password on it in the live settings.
live.setupNoteDns: Next: create the DNS records shown on the app's page, then check DNS.
live.created: Live site set up. Point the domain at the server, then check DNS.
live.editDescription: A new domain or name is checked again in DNS before the next release to live.
live.editRunning: The live site is running: stop it first to change its domain or names. Access can be changed now.
live.accessPublicHelp: Anyone can open it; search engines may index it. Usual for a site that has launched.
live.accessPasswordHelp: Visitors need a username and password. Useful before launch.
live.namesResetDns: Changing the names checks DNS again right away; a release to live waits until it is ok.
live.dnsPending: The domain does not point at the server yet. Create the DNS records below, then check DNS.
live.releaseDescription: Pick a version that ran in the preview. Exactly that commit is built on the live server and switched on at {domain}; if a step fails, the version live now keeps running.
live.releasePick: Versions that ran in the preview, newest first
live.releaseNone: No version has run in the preview yet. Deploy the preview first and check it there.
live.releaseDnsFirst: The domain does not point at the server yet. Check DNS first: a release to live waits until it is ok.
live.releaseAudited: You confirm with your password and authenticator code. The release is recorded in the audit log.
live.removeHelp: Removes the live site at {domain} from its server with its files and its database. The preview stays.
live.removeConfirm: Remove the live site at {domain}? Its files and its database are deleted from the server. The preview stays. This cannot be undone.
live.removing: Removing the live site from its server…
live.releaseEnvChanged: {count, plural, one {This live variable changed} other {These # live variables changed}} since the version live now. The release brings the new values:
live.removeDump: A final dump of the live database is kept on the server for 30 days.
live.planBackupHelp: The live database is backed up before anything changes. If the backup fails, the release stops and nothing changes.
live.planNoDatabase: No database: the new version starts in its own slot and traffic switches over once it answers.
live.planExpand: The migration only adds (expand): it runs while the version live now keeps serving. A release that says expand but drops, renames or narrows anything is refused before it changes anything.
live.planBreaking: The migration may change existing data (breaking): visitors see a short maintenance page while the database migrates, then the new version takes over.
live.planUnknownHelp: This version's wfos.json is read when it builds: expand runs without downtime, breaking (the default) shows a maintenance page while it migrates.
live.planGraceHelp: {minutes, plural, one {The version live now keeps running for a minute after the switch, so a rollback in that time is immediate.} other {The version live now keeps running for # minutes after the switch, so a rollback in that time is immediate.}}

dns.title: Domain and DNS
dns.help: At the client's DNS provider, create these records for every name, then check. It can take a few minutes, sometimes hours, before public DNS sees a change.
dns.okHelp: Every name points at the server. The live site can be released.
dns.okToast: DNS is ok: every name points at the server.

summary.wrong: Some names point at another address. Correct the records and check again.
summary.missing: Some names have no record yet. Create them and check again in a few minutes.
summary.error: Public DNS did not answer. Try again in a moment.

dns.notChecked: Not checked yet. Check DNS to see the server's address and what each name answers.
dns.noServerAddress: The server's own address could not be found in public DNS. Check the server's host in Settings → Servers, then check again.
dns.certificate: At the first release to live, Let's Encrypt issues the certificate for {domain}. It needs DNS to be ok.
dns.certificateWithAliases: At the first release to live, Let's Encrypt issues one certificate for {domain} and {aliases}; those names redirect to {domain}. It needs DNS to be ok.

backups.title: Database backups
backups.liveHelp: Taken before every release to live, once a day, before a restore and whenever you ask. The newest are kept on the server; older daily ones are pruned.
backups.previewHelp: Taken before a release that migrates, before a restore and whenever you ask. The preview has its own database, separate from live.
backups.queued: Backup queued. It shows up here when it is done.
backups.empty: No backups yet. The first one is taken before the next release with a database, or now.
backups.stale: The last backup is from {ago}: the daily backup did not run. Back up now and check the server.
backups.staleNever: This live site has no backup yet. Back up now.
backups.restoreOwnerOnly: Only the Owner restores a database.
backups.serverOnly: Backups are kept on the app server only: no offsite copy is configured. If the server is lost, its backups are lost with it.
backups.restoreDescription: Put the database of {domain} back to this backup.
backups.restoreLoss: Everything written to the database since {time} is lost.
backups.restoreSafety: The current database is backed up first (before restore), so this can be undone with that backup.
backups.restoreMaintenance: Visitors see the maintenance page while it restores; the site comes back on its own once it answers again.
backups.restoreDowntime: The preview stops while it restores and starts again on its own.
backups.restoreAudited: You confirm with your password and authenticator code. The restore is recorded in the audit log.
backups.restoreQueued: Restore queued. The site shows the maintenance page until it is done.

window.title: Release window
window.help: When releases to live may start. Rollbacks are always possible, also outside the window.
window.anyTimeHelp: A release to live can start whenever the Owner confirms it.
window.onlyWindowHelp: Releases wait for quiet hours, e.g. at night when few visitors are on the site.
window.overnight: Runs past midnight: it ends at {end} the next day.
window.sameTimes: From and until are the same: the whole day counts.
window.stepUp: Changing the release window is confirmed with your password and authenticator code.
window.closedNow: Release window: {window}. Closed now: a release to live waits.
window.releaseWaits: Outside the release window: a release to live waits until it opens. Rollbacks are still possible.

uptime.title: Uptime
uptime.pausedStopped: The live site is stopped, so it is not checked.
uptime.pausedMaintenance: The maintenance page is showing, so the site is not checked meanwhile.
uptime.stripLabel: The last 24 hours in 5-minute checks: {checked} checks, {failed} failed.
uptime.certSoon: {days, plural, =0 {Certificate expires today ({date})} one {Certificate expires in # day ({date})} other {Certificate expires in # days ({date})}}: automatic renewal is late
uptime.certExpired: Certificate expired on {date}: visitors see a security warning
uptime.certUnknown: Certificate not read yet (at the next good check)
uptime.noIncidents: No incidents in the last 30 days.
uptime.incidentOngoing: {minutes, plural, one {Down for # minute so far} other {Down for # minutes so far}}

unmerged.title: Not in {base} yet ({count})
unmerged.hint: Finished work that a deploy of {base} does not include and the next task does not start from. Open a task to merge it or leave it out.
unmerged.others: After one of these is merged, the others usually need the employee to bring them up to date first (they were built on an older {base}).

testUsers.title: Test accounts
testUsers.description: One account per role on this preview, made by the app's testUsers command (wfos-app.json) after each preview release, or added here. The browser tester signs in with them.
testUsers.empty: No test accounts yet. Add a testUsers command to wfos-app.json (it gets the shared password in $WFOS_TEST_PASSWORD and prints the accounts as JSON), or add one here.
testUsers.removeAutoConfirm: Remove {label}? The app makes it again on its next preview release while its testUsers command still does.

fields.label: Name
fields.passwordShared: Empty: the preview's shared test password.
fields.passwordNeeded: This preview has no shared test password yet: give this account its own.

testUsers.audited: Every password shown is recorded in the audit log.

tests.title: App tests
tests.description: A tester employee uses the preview in a real browser, like its users: signs in as each role, walks the flows, and reports findings with steps and screenshots. Started by a person, never on every release.
tests.started: Test started: the tester is on it
tests.focusPlaceholder: e.g. the purchase request → approval flow, and that a requester cannot approve
tests.rolesHint: None ticked: the tester covers every role.
tests.noAccounts: This preview has no test accounts: the tester can only check what a visitor sees.
tests.costNote: The test runs as a task of the tester and uses its budget.
tests.fixFrom: Found by the app test of {app} (commit {commit}).

docs.title: Documents
docs.importPrd: Import a PRD from a task
docs.prdStale: {count, plural, one {# preview release since this PRD was approved: it may be out of date.} other {# preview releases since this PRD was approved: it may be out of date.}}

empty.prd: No PRD yet. Import one written in a task, or ask an employee to write it.
empty.flow: No business flow yet: the process for business people, with a diagram per process.
empty.test_guide: No test guide yet: the steps to try each role on the preview.
empty.deck: No presentation yet: slides for a prospect, with screenshots of the latest app test.

docs.approved: Approved: this is the version people work from
docs.rejectConfirm: Reject this draft? The approved version stays.

askExplain.prd: Brings the PRD in line with the app: what was built since the approved version, changes asked for, what is still open. It becomes a draft next to the approved PRD.
askExplain.flow: The process for business people, with a diagram per process, from the approved PRD.
askExplain.test_guide: Step-by-step checks per role for the people who try the preview, from the PRD and the test accounts.
askExplain.deck: Slides for a prospect, built on the business flow, with screenshots of the latest app test (run one first for screenshots).

docs.asked: Asked: the task is on the board
docs.noCandidates: No PRD has been written in a task of this workspace yet.

modules.title: Modules
modules.empty: No modules yet. Split the app into modules (e.g. Orders, Invoices, Reports): each gets its own PRD and is built on its own, in this app's repository.
modules.noRepository: This app has no repository: modules can be planned, but not built.
modules.buildingNow: Building now (one module at a time per app):

explain.draft: No approved PRD yet: ask an employee to write it, then approve it.
explain.ready: The PRD is approved: the module can be built.
explain.building: A build or change is running. It publishes the usual way: push and preview approvals, then the merge.
explain.in_review: Work was pushed and waits to be merged into the main branch (the task's Code tab).
explain.merged: The work is in the main branch, not on LIVE yet.
explain.live: The version LIVE runs contains this module's work.
explain.paused: Paused: nothing new is built until it is resumed.
explain.dropped: Dropped: kept for its history, nothing is built.

modules.writingPrdLong: An employee is writing the first PRD.
modules.pending: {what} waits until the module that is being built now is done (requested {at}).
modules.dropConfirm: Drop the module "{name}"? Nothing more is built for it; its history stays.
modules.removeConfirm: Remove the module "{name}" and its PRD versions?
modules.rejectConfirm: Reject this draft? The approved version stays.
modules.name: Name
modules.slugHelp: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Folders and branches follow it; it is fixed once the module was built.
modules.slugFixed: Fixed: the module was built with this name.
modules.summaryPlaceholder: Who uses it, what they do with it, what it must not do…
modules.addedWriting: Module added: its PRD is being written
modules.askPrdExplain: The employee writes a new version from the app's PRD and the other modules. It is a draft until an Admin or the Owner approves it.
modules.askNote: What should it cover or change? (optional)
modules.prdAsked: Asked: the draft appears here and in Needs a decision
modules.buildExplain: A code task in the app's repository, from PRD v{version}. One module is built at a time: if another is being built, this one waits and starts by itself.
modules.changeExplain: A code task that changes this module (PRD v{version} stays the reference unless the request changes it). One at a time per app.
modules.workStarted: Started: follow it on the task
modules.workQueued: Waiting: it starts when "{task}" is done
modules.registerExplain: Work on this repository that no module claims yet. Pick the task that built this module: its pushes and merges count for it, without building it again.
modules.registerNone: No unclaimed work on this repository.
modules.importExplain: A PRD written as a task deliverable becomes the module's next PRD version (a draft to approve).
modules.importNone: No PRD deliverables in this workspace yet.
